title: 第二卷十二洛神祭第二卷十二彩蛋圆满篇

那枚银戒，破军戴了一千三百年。
戒面被指腹摩挲得温润，星图边缘已模糊，唯有正中的破军星位，因日日触碰而愈发明亮。像有人用千年时光，将一颗星磨成了灯。
他总记得那句话。
——若他日星落长安，请君持此寻我。
他寻了一千三百年。
从长安到洛阳，从盛唐到残唐，从人间到忘川。他在每一条她可能走过的街道驻足，在每一座她可能停过的桥头等待，在每一场她可能看过的雪里伸出手，接住融化的六角冰晶。
都没有她。
后来他想，也许她说的“他日”不是某一天，而是某一世。也许她的魂魄早已渡过忘川，饮过孟婆汤，在某户寻常人家做了寻常女子，织布、浣衣、嫁人、生子，安然老去，葬在寻常的山岗。
那也很好。
他这样告诉自己。只要她不再困于那年的渭水之滨，只要她不必以身为舟渡尽苍生，只要她能在某处寻常地活着、笑着、老去——
那便很好。
可他还是忍不住要寻。
寻了一千三百年，从化神初期寻到化神巅峰，从凡人寻成传说。寻到后来，他已分不清自己是在寻她，还是在寻那个曾为一人怦然心动的少年。
今夜，渭水有风。
破军独立岸边，玄衣被暮色浸透。他看着河水东流，想起一千三百年前，也是这样的风，这样的水，这样将暗未暗的天。
她站在他面前，披着蓑衣，发间簪一朵新摘的洛神花。
“将军要走了？”她问。
他点头。北疆有战事，他必须去。

她笑了笑，将一枚银戒放入他掌心：“那这个给你。”
“这是什么？”
“星戒。”她说，“若有一日，将军在长安城头看见流星坠落，便是我来寻你了。”
他低头看那戒面，北斗七星熠熠生辉，正中的破军星位尤其明亮。他那时不知，这枚戒是她用半身修为凝成，戒面上的星，是真的从天上摘下来的。
他更不知，那是他最后一次见她。
三个月后，北疆大捷。他策马回长安，满城都在传：渭水出了妖龙，洛神庙的那位姑娘，以身祭水，封龙脉于河底。
他赶到渭水时，水面平静如镜，没有她，没有妖龙，没有半点她存在过的痕迹。
只有岸边一朵枯萎的洛神花。
他在那里站了七天七夜。
第七夜，渭水下起了雨。雨水打在他脸上，混入他眼中，他分不清那是天在哭，还是他在哭。
后来他才知道，她祭水那日，手里握着他临别时赠的青锋——那剑原是他想送她的定情信，却因羞于启齿，只说是“防身之用”。
她握着那柄剑，沉入水底。
剑锋刺入龙脉的那一刻，她轻声说：
“萧将军，若他日星落长安，我怕是去不了了。你来寻我，好不好？”
千年后，他仍在寻。
---
破军到来后的第七日，永珍额间的印记，终于无法再隐藏。
那印记初时极淡，像一痕月牙浸在水中，晨起暮落间时隐时现。永珍用脂粉遮掩，用碎发覆额，对着铜镜练习了无数遍若无其事的表情。
但她瞒不过杨思纯。
他不问，只是在她疲累时递来热茶，在她怔忡时握住她的手，在每一个她以为他未察觉的瞬间，用那种沉默的、包容的目光，将她所有强撑的坚强轻轻接住。

这夜，长安又落雨。
永珍独坐窗前，指尖抚过额间愈发清晰的印记。那印记已从月牙蔓延成花瓣状——六瓣，每一瓣都像极了洛神花。
她终于想起那些纠缠她许久的梦了。
梦里总有一道背影，披蓑衣，簪洛神花，立于渭水之滨。那女子从不回头，只望着滔滔东流的河水，轻声问：
“你可愿承我血脉，代我守这长安千年？”

That silver ring has been worn by Po Jun for thirteen hundred years.
The surface of the ring was warmed by the fingertips, and the edges of the star map were blurred. Only the Pojun star in the center became brighter and brighter with every passing day. It's like someone spent thousands of years grinding a star into a lamp.
He always remembers that sentence.
——If the stars set in Chang'an one day, please hold this and look for me.
He searched for thirteen hundred years.
From Chang'an to Luoyang, from the prosperous Tang Dynasty to the end of the Tang Dynasty, from the human world to Wangchuan. He stopped at every street she might have walked, waited at every bridge she might have stopped at, stretched out his hand in every snow she might have seen, and caught the melting hexagonal ice crystals.
None of her.
Later he thought that maybe the "other day" she was talking about was not a certain day, but a certain life. Maybe her soul has already crossed the River of Forgetfulness, drank Meng Po Soup, lived as an ordinary woman in an ordinary family, weaved cloth, washed clothes, married, had children, grew old peacefully, and was buried on an ordinary hill.
That's also good.
He told himself this. As long as she is no longer trapped on the shore of the Weishui River that year, as long as she does not have to use her body to sail across the world, as long as she can live, laugh, and grow old somewhere normally——
That's good.
But he still couldn't help but look for it.
After searching for 1,300 years, he found it from the early stage of becoming a god to the peak of becoming a god, and from a mortal to a legend. After he found her, he couldn't tell whether he was looking for her or the young man whose heart had been so moved by someone.
Tonight, there is wind on the Wei River.
Po Jun was standing alone on the shore, and Xuan Yi was soaked in the dusk. He looked at the river flowing eastward and remembered that thirteen hundred years ago, there was the same wind, such water, and such a dark sky.
She stood in front of him, wearing a coir raincoat and a newly picked rose flower in her hair.
"The general is leaving?" she asked.
He nodded. There was a war in northern Xinjiang and he had to go.
She smiled and put a silver ring into his palm: "Then this is for you."
"What is this?"
"Star Ring." She said, "If one day, the general sees a meteor falling from the top of Chang'an City, I will be the one looking for you."
He lowered his head and looked at the ring surface. The Big Dipper was shining brightly, and the Pojun star in the center was particularly bright. He didn't know at the time that this ring was made with half of her body, and the stars on the ring were really plucked from the sky.
He didn't even know that that was the last time he saw her.
Three months later, a great victory was achieved in Northern Xinjiang. He rode back to Chang'an, and word spread throughout the city that a demonic dragon emerged from the Wei River. The girl from the Luo Temple sacrificed her body to the water and sealed the dragon's veins at the bottom of the river.
When he arrived at the Weishui River, the water was as calm as a mirror. There was no her, no demonic dragon, and no trace of her existence.
There was only a withered rosette on the shore.
He stood there seven days and seven nights.
On the seventh night, it started to rain on the Wei River. The rain hit his face and mixed into his eyes. He couldn't tell whether it was the sky crying or him crying.
Later he found out that on the day she offered the water sacrifice, she was holding the Qingfeng sword he had given her when she was leaving - that sword was originally a love letter he wanted to give her, but because he was too shy to say it, he only said it was "for self-defense."
She held the sword and sank to the bottom of the water.
The moment the sword edge pierced the dragon's veins, she whispered:
"General Xiao, if the sun sets in Chang'an one day, I'm afraid I won't be able to go. Come and look for me, okay?"
Thousands of years later, he is still searching.
---
On the seventh day after Po Jun arrived, the mark on Yongzhen's forehead could no longer be hidden.
The mark was very faint at first, like a crescent moon soaked in water, appearing and disappearing in the morning and evening. Yongzhen covered her face with powder, covered her forehead with broken hair, and practiced her nonchalant expression countless times in front of the bronze mirror.
But she couldn't hide it from Yang Sichun.
He didn't ask, he just handed her hot tea when she was tired, held her hand when she was stunned, and used his silent and tolerant eyes to gently catch all her strength at every moment when she thought he wasn't aware of it.
That night, it rained again in Chang'an.
Yongzhen sat alone in front of the window, her fingertips touching the increasingly clear mark on her forehead. The mark has spread from the crescent moonIt extends into the shape of petals - six petals, each petal is very much like a rosette.
She finally remembered the dreams that had haunted her for so long.
In dreams, there is always a figure from behind, wearing a coir raincoat and a hairpin of Luo Shenhua, standing on the shore of the Wei River. The woman never looked back, only looked at the river flowing eastward, and asked softly:
"Are you willing to inherit my bloodline and guard Chang'an for a thousand years on my behalf?"
